parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: A sample of a radioactive isotope contains $N$ nuclei of the isotope at time $T$. At time $(T + \Delta T)$, the sample contains $(N - \Delta N)$ nuclei of the isotope. The time interval $\Delta T$ is short.
parts.text: Use the symbols $N$, $\Delta N$, $T$ and $\Delta T$ to give expressions for:

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: the average activity of the sample during the time $\Delta T$

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: the probability of decay of a nucleus in the time $\Delta T$

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: the decay constant $\lambda$ of the isotope.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The isotope polonium-208 ($^{208}_{84}\text{Po}$) is radioactive and decays to form lead-204 ($^{204}_{82}\text{Pb}$). The nuclear equation for this decay is $$^{208}_{84}\text{Po} \rightarrow ^{204}_{82}\text{Pb} + ^{4}_{2}\text{He}.$$ Data for nuclear masses are given in Fig. 12.1.
| {{header}} {{blank}} | {{header}} mass / u |
| --- | --- |
| $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ | 4.002603 |
| $^{204}_{82}\text{Pb}$ | 203.973043 |
| $^{208}_{84}\text{Po}$ | 207.981245 |

Fig. 12.1

parts.label: bi
parts.text:
(b)(i) Determine, for the decay of one nucleus of polonium-208:

1. the change, in $\text{u}$, of the mass

2. the total energy, in $\text{pJ}$, released.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The polonium-208 nucleus is initially stationary. The initial kinetic energy of the $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ nucleus ($\alpha$-particle) is found to be less than the energy calculated in (i) part 2.

Suggest two possible reasons for this difference.
